cover.title: They filmed downwind of the bomb

lines.text: Hollywood shot a movie in the desert... and years later, almost half the people who made it had cancer.
1954. Howard Hughes' studio is filming The Conqueror, a big budget epic starring John Wayne.
They shoot near St. George, Utah, in a red rock canyon called Snow Canyon.
About a hundred and forty miles away is the Nevada Test Site. Where the United States was setting off atomic bombs in the open air.
The year before, a test nicknamed Dirty Harry sent a cloud of fallout drifting over southern Utah.
Cast and crew spent weeks in that dust. The studio even shipped tons of the dirt back to Hollywood for reshoots.
By 1980, a magazine counted ninety one of the two hundred and twenty people who worked on the film with cancer. Forty six had died of it.
John Wayne. Susan Hayward. Agnes Moorehead. The director, Dick Powell. Wayne was also a heavy smoker, and scientists still argue about the link.
Hughes reportedly felt so guilty, he bought up every copy of the film and kept it off TV for years.
Would you have taken the job? Comment not worth it... and sleep tight, partner.
